Messages.Author: Oortje
Messages.Body:
When i play Bima and move and agent of power to it, does this wording means it is in play? And therefor contest?

Bima
Ally
Follower of Set
1 blood
Ghoul with 2 life. 2 strength, 1 bleed.
When this Bima enters play, move a master: Discipline card to it from your hand or burn this Bima. The Bima may play cards that require the basic level of that Discipline as a vampire.

Agent of Power
Master
Master: Discipline. Trifle. Unique.
Put this card on a vampire you control and choose a Discipline. This vampire gains 1 level of that Discipline. Burn this card during your discard phase

Have a cold long night,
Jeroen van Oort
Dutch National Coördinator

Messages.Author: jamesatzephyr
Messages.Body:
> Oortje wrote:
> When i play Bima and move and agent of power to it, does this wording means it is in play? And therefor contest?
>
It's unique and will contest any other Agent of Powers that are in play. (Meaning you can't voluntarily self-contest.)

[LSJ 20071003]

Also as stated in that post, the Agent of Power (by its own card text) burns at the end of the turn.

> LSJ wrote:
> It is unique, yes.
> So you cannot play another one while you control that one.
> But that one will burn during your discard phase, by card text on Agent of Power.
> ...
> And then, on your next turn, you can play another Agent of Power on a new Bima
> (since you won't be self-contesting).
>
However, the point that Bima retains use of the discipline (not quoted above) is wrong, and is reversed a little later:

[LSJ 20071006]

> LSJ wrote:
> REVERSAL: Bima's "that Discipline" refers to the card on Bima, just as the
> Satyr's "that card" refers to the card on Satyr.
>
> If the card is no longer there, then the effect cannot be used.
>
